correctness.rationale: The endpoint spectral sine weights are all nonzero, yielding a cyclic space with one supported vector per distinct sampled phase. The monitored-return formula is reconstructed by contraction of Q and the exact telescoping identity sum Q^t P Q*^t=I. A rational relation between positive prime-path energies would give a polynomial divisible by Phi_(2p), but its missing central coefficient contradicts the nonzero central cyclotomic coefficient. Thus spectral gaps indexed by distinct coefficient vectors have irrational ratios. There are m^2 gap types and each sampling resonance merges one or two and no more spectral pairs. Therefore the three exact mean-return counts hold for all positive times. Direct Lyapunov checks (43 cases) corroborate only; they are not the proof. Boundaries p=3, every positive integer ladder multiple, and tau>0 are explicit.

value.rationale: Quantum first-detection return time jumps at exact spectral phase resonances, an intrinsic physical observable. For every prime path length the theorem locates every exceptional positive interval, proves that simultaneous distinct resonances cannot occur, counts m^2 disjoint ladders, and gives the complete three-branch mean (with an empty third branch at the smallest odd prime). This natural uniform classification needs an exact cyclotomic lemma and resolves more than one small parameter slice, numerical table, or restatement of general quantization. No experimental advantage or broad graph generalization is asserted.
